answer: To deter Sybil attacks in an agent economy, nodes authenticate peers via photoacoustic unclonable tokens. Validators pulse light onto a microscopic pigment tag deposited by a nanolithographic quill, recording the ultrasonic echo response. An adversary cannot virtualize nodes, incurring non-trivial microfabrication hardware costs per identity. However, surface abrasion and temperature fluctuations alter acoustic impedance over time, triggering false authentication rejections.
